pos.personaBrief: Spain had 68.2% possession at Euro 2012 and Del Bosque's 'greatest concern is control' (Irish Times); counters were slow and he was patient against deep teams.

pro.personaBrief: Spain avoided long balls (FourFourTwo), built short with a double pivot, and he said possession without depth is pointless; still pragmatic when a pass is on.

est.personaBrief: Spain combined in tight spaces with a false nine and a double pivot, and he adapted tactically to his players; roles were clear but fluid.

lar.personaBrief: 4-6-0 at Euro 2012, double pivot and Zidane as the tip of the diamond put the best players centrally, though full-backs and Villa/Pedro gave some width.

blo.personaBrief: Spain pressed high (FourFourTwo, Bleacher Report) and he said the team works to pressure and win the ball back; Madrid's back three was a one-off adaptation.

mar.personaBrief: No marking evidence; Spain and Madrid played organised, space-based defending without dedicated man-markers, so zone is the default.

pla.personaBrief: He said there is no magic formula and the plan follows the available players; he changed shape (back three at Old Trafford, 4-6-0 against Italy) but kept the control identity.

res.personaBrief: A pragmatic winner: 'if you lose it all comes down like a house of cards', defensive order and one goal per knockout game in 2010, but with a control-based, pleasant style.

sis.personaBrief: A man-manager who gave stars roles in a balanced collective; Zidane got a new position, but Del Bosque valued team players like Busquets, Alonso and Makelele.

jog.personaBrief: His teams were technical (Spain, Zidane, Xabi, Busquets) and valued passing midfielders over physical ones, though pressing intensity mattered.

bas.personaBrief: Built on a base of veterans (Hierro, Redondo, Raul, Casillas) and kept loyalty to Casillas; experience first, though he trusted cantera players.

lid.personaBrief: The 'quiet man' who said human relations come above competition, good atmosphere and accepting each player as he is, with equal treatment and one sending-off in 114 matches.
